selected.title: The station that counts the water
selected.texas_link: UT San Antonio researchers in Bexar County built a prototype street-level flood warning station. The announcement names no installation site, so the film draws San Antonio streets as an illustration and says prototype.

movement.actor: University of Texas at San Antonio
movement.action: published a field-ready prototype flood warning node that runs its machine learning model on the chip
movement.object: a solar powered street-level station with four optical water-level sensors at different heights

selected.why_today: UT San Antonio published the prototype on September 8th, 2026. The Docket carries it as a decided prototype announcement, and its mechanism can be drawn from the university's own page and honestly limited.
selected.consequence: The node judges flood risk on the device, sends warnings by long range radio, and a central hub builds a web dashboard of predicted flood paths for emergency responders.
selected.application_change: A flood gauge that needs grid power and a network becomes a self-powered station that judges flood risk on its own chip.
selected.counter_image: The 98.82 percent is validation accuracy from initial assessments after training, and the article reports no field or street result. The announcement names no place that has installed a station.
selected.earned_take: The university reports a parts cost of roughly $150 to $220 for one prototype station and a validation figure, but it names no place that uses one.

agency.next_step: Chen Pan is pursuing patent protection, and the team aims to refine the design into a weatherized commercial product. No dates are given.
agency.who_can_act: The UT San Antonio research team builds and tests it. The team names small coastal municipalities, homeowners' associations, agricultural operations and industrial sites as possible users. A Texas Coastal Management Program grant from NOAA funded part of the work.

sources.note: UT San Antonio Today, September 8th, 2026, Audrey Gray
Texas AI Docket record tx-2026-0141 with ten verified quote claims
Texas General Land Office Coastal Management Program project page, started December 1st, 2023

filmability.viewer_question: Can a flood station judge rising street water with no power line and no cell tower?
filmability.opening_action: An illustrated solar station beside a street. Water rises past four sensor marks at different heights. Disclosed as Illustration.
filmability.mechanism: Input: four optical water-level sensors plus temperature, humidity, light and rain sensing. Transformation: a compressed model on the chip judges flood risk locally. Result: a radio warning goes to a hub and a dashboard of predicted flood paths. Limit: validation accuracy only and no named installation.
filmability.human_consequence: Emergency responders and residents of street-level flood-prone blocks. No affected resident or responder is named in any source.
filmability.source_limit: The design and accuracy claims rest on the university's own account. The accuracy figure is from initial assessments after training. No installed site, no field result and no price for a finished product are published.
three_key_images: The solar station with four sensor heights, drawn as an illustration
Water crossing the four marks one at a time while the chip lights a local risk judgment
A radio pulse to a hub and a dashboard of predicted flood paths beside the card that says no installed site is named

asset_leads.relevant_image: University article photographs of the prototype were not located or downloaded.
asset_leads.what_it_proves: Nothing the film needs. The article is the source for the design.
asset_leads.inspection: Text read through a fetch summary. No image downloaded.
asset_leads.rights_basis: None established. No reuse licence found, so no photograph is admitted.

action_support.pictured_action: Water rises at a street-side post past four sensor marks at different heights.
action_support.scope_fit: Disclosed explanatory diagram of the design the university describes. It shows no installed site, no real street and no measured reading.
action_support.relationship: The university says the prototype carries four optical water-level sensors mounted at varying heights.

action_support.pictured_action: Sensor readings enter a chip and a local risk judgment lights without any line to a server.
action_support.scope_fit: Disclosed explanatory diagram of where the model runs. It shows no real model internals and no real output.
action_support.relationship: The university says the on-device AI evaluates sensor data to predict localized imminent flood risk without relying on a central server.

action_support.pictured_action: A radio pulse reaches a hub and a dashboard map of predicted flood paths opens for responders, beside a card reading no installed site named.
action_support.scope_fit: Disclosed explanatory diagram of the relationship the university describes. It shows no real dashboard and no real responder.
action_support.relationship: The university says a central hub aggregates data from nodes into a web dashboard with predictive flood-path maps for emergency responders. It names no deployment.

visual_stakes.affected_group: Emergency responders and residents on street-level flood-prone blocks in Texas towns and cities.
visual_stakes.physical_subject: a solar flood station with four water-level sensors at different heights
visual_stakes.visible_change: water crosses the four sensor marks in turn, the chip judges the risk, and a radio pulse leaves for a hub
visual_stakes.consequence: A dashboard of predicted flood paths for emergency responders, per the university's description. No place is named as using it.
visual_stakes.opening_question: Can a flood station judge rising street water with no power line and no cell tower?
visual_stakes.answer: The design says yes, on its own solar power. The proof so far is validation accuracy, not a street.
visual_stakes.asset_fit: Two fresh authored source groups, a flood station hero and a street and hub support group, shared by two complete treatments. Diagram and illustration only, no footage and no real site.
visual_stakes.affected_person: An illustrated emergency worker watching a dashboard and a driver on a street-level block that floods first, both disclosed illustration
